newsitem.title: UK: UK's Offer raps suppliers on discriminatory deals.
newsitem.headline: UK's Offer raps suppliers on discriminatory deals.

text.p: Britain's electricity industry watchdog Offer on Thursday called on suppliers to stop offering supply arrangements which could lock in franchise customers ahead of 1998 when the market will be opened to competition.

In a statement, the watchdog told companies not to offer contracts to customers in the under 100 kiloWatt market which might "restrict or distort competition after 1998" or which discriminated between franchise customers should not be offered.
It added that any customers who already had such contracts should be allowed to terminate them from April 1998 without penalty.

The watchdog is concerned that some suppliers might be offering contracts to franchise customers -- which tend to be sizeable small businesses such as individual factories -- with special terms in order to keep them past 1998.

"This might involve offering a discounted price now to customers with sites in both the under and over 100 kW markets, or...to under 100 kW customers who agree to sign longer term contracts which extend beyond 1998," Offer said in a statement.
Local public electricity suppliers (PESs), which include regional electricity companies (Recs), are the only firms which can offer special terms such as these, Offer said.
Offer is also concerned that any special deals might be available only to selected customers or might be subsidised through charges to other users.
It said it would ensure that "discounts to certain franchise customers are not at the expense of other customers."
Offer has asked PESs to tell it of any such contracts or if any have been offered and if so, to provide details.
"We are trying to ensure that there is fair and equal access to contracts on offer," a spokeswoman for Offer said.
